newsitem.title: PERU: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO, CRISTAL DRAW IN LIBERTADORES FIRST LEG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUZEIRO, CRISTAL DRAW IN LIBERTADORES FIRST LEG.

text.p: Peru's giant-killers Sporting Cristal ran out of steam during a tight 0-0 draw Wedensday against Brazil's Cruzeiro in the first leg of South America's premier club competition, the Libertadores Cup.
A fired-up Cristal harried from the outset, with strikers Julinho and Bonnet running tirelessly but failing to make much headway against the more highly-rated Brazilian club's cool defence.
Urged on by a capacity 45,000 crowd at Lima's National Stadium, the Peruvians came closest to securing a crucial home lead in a last-minute goalmouth scramble.
But it was Cruzeiro who cut out the best chances in fast breaks from the back, forcing several dramatic one-on-one saves from Cristal goalkeeper Julio Cesar Balerio.

The Brazilians were happy, however, to defend for most of the game, coping easily with Cristal's high-ball approach. The Peruvians held most of the possession but missed the punch of suspended stars Prince Amoako of Ghana and local goalscoring hero Julio Rivera.

The result left Cruzeiro firm favourites to lift the trophy at next Wednesday's second leg in Brazil, and dampened Sporting Cristal's hopes of becoming the first Peruvian club to win the title in its 38-year history.

Cristal, who recorded shock wins over Argentina's powerhouses Velez Sarsfield and Racing Club earlier in the tournament, were the first Peruvian team to reach the finals in 25 years after another Lima club, Universitario, lost to Independiente of Argentina in 1972.
Peru lines up with Ecuador, Venezuela and Bolivia as the countries never to have claimed the trophy.

Cruzeiro were playing in the final for the third time, but their last appearance at this stage was two decades ago when they won in 1976. The Brazilians will miss their powerful forward Cleisson in next week's second after he was sent off for a clumsy foul in the game's dying minutes.

Cristal - Julio Cesar Balerio, Marcelo Asteggiano, Manuel Marengo, Miguel Rebosio (Eric Torres, 54), Martin Vasquez (Andres Mendoza, 62), Nolberto Solano, Pedro Garay, Alfredo Carmona (Alex Magallanes, 62), Jorge Soto, Alberto Bonnet y Julinho.
Cruzeiro - Dida, Vitor, Gelson, Gottardo, Nonato, Fabinho, Ricardinho, Donizete, Palinha, Cleisson y Marcelo (Da Silva, 77).
